set.approach: Follow the Dry Horse Creek trail up to the saddle between Wet Horse and Dry Horse creeks, then walk west across to the foot of the Eocene tower. The route begins in the saddle between Brokeback Mountain and the Eocene and then angles up and across the formation's north side.
set.descent_text: From the summit platform, walk a short way east and rappel to an exposed ledge. A long rappel straight down from there reaches the ledge at the foot of the sixth pitch, and the remainder of the descent is rappelling the route itself.

review.notes: Approach from area page and route Location line; descent from route page. Rappel counts left out.

set.approach: The route starts at the notch between Buck Mountain and Static Peak, reached by climbing snow. Begin just left of the notch and work up a short stretch of loose fourth-class rock before the crack climbing near the ridgeline begins.
set.descent_text: From the top of the tower at the end of the roped climbing, downclimb fourth-class ground to the col, then wander up fourth-class terrain to the summit. Early in the season the descent of the east face is a steep, exposed snow slope that needs care.

review.notes: Route page Location and description; one source.

set.approach: Hike up the south fork of Avalanche Canyon to the foot of the north face. The start is at the base of the face below an obvious crack and chimney system. Early in the season expect moderate snow climbing and wet rock on the lower route.
set.descent_text: The route tops out a short distance below the summit. The descent is down the east slopes.

review.notes: Route page; area page confirms south fork of Avalanche Canyon for the north face.

set.approach: Walk north from Pahaska on service roads and ski trails, cross the creek, and follow the Crow Creek trail west. When due north of the peak, turn south through brush to a meadow with log crossings, then follow a faint trail to the big avalanche gully below the north ridge. Stay just right of the gully to avoid the worst brush, pass a cliff band, and climb the steep couloir of snow or talus to the ridge; an ice axe and crampons are needed when it holds snow. Traverse southwest across the base of the ridge on third- and fourth-class ledges to the start, a ledge southwest of the crest.
set.descent_text: Descend the standard east face rappel line, which uses slung horns and pins for anchors.

review.notes: Approach from area page plus route Location; descent from route page.

set.descent_text: Descend the standard east face rappel line. Anchors are nuts, pins and slung horns.

review.notes: Descent stated on this route page and the north ridge page. Approach skipped: no source places the start of this face.

set.approach: Head up from Deep Lake, or from Black Joe Lake, to the west side of the dome, the side that faces Temple Lake and Temple Peak. Near the middle of that face is a clean left-facing dihedral, where the route starts. The base of the dome is a long day-hike from the Big Sandy trailhead for a light party, and longer with a heavy pack.
set.descent_text: Walk off south toward Deep Lake. The ground is third class and somewhat slabby in places.

review.notes: Route page; area page for access.

set.approach: Follow the Garnet Canyon trail nearly to the platform camping area. Find Open Book, then look one buttress east across a large talus gully to Almost Arete, whose face carries a large white and yellow square slab called the Postage Stamp. Climb loose talus directly up to the base. The route starts beneath a huge black roof just east of the Postage Stamp, well west of the long Satisfaction Crack that bounds the buttress. There is no climbers' trail.
set.descent_text: From the summit of the arete, go east down fourth-class slabs to an anchor on a big tree limb, then rappel a short way onto grassy slopes. Traverse to skier's right to the ridge crest and follow third- and second-class ground back to Surprise Lake.

review.notes: Route page Location and Descent text.

set.approach: From the meadow in the cirque directly below Warbonnet, hike the talus straight up to the foot of the spire. The first pitch starts in a recess at the left end of the spire, reached by scrambling.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route with double ropes.

set.approach: The route begins from the saddle on the northeast side of the peak, where the Gannett and Gooseneck glaciers meet. Climbers reach it over glacier, either by climbing the Gooseneck on snow or ice, or by coming around the Gannett Glacier from the north and west. From the saddle the line goes up the ridge over fourth-class ledges littered with loose rock toward a reddish spire.
set.descent_text: Descend the Gooseneck Glacier and couloir.

set.approach: Hike over the col between Haystack Mountain and Temple Spire; the buttress is obvious from there. The route starts from the base below the buttress, where a prominent right-leaning splitter crack runs up the face.

From Clear Lake, follow the trail and scramble across glaciated terrain to the base of the mountain. The chimney is an unmistakable gash in the middle stretch of the long west face, directly to the right of Central Corner. Do not confuse it with Grassy Crack, a shallower chimney system to the left of Central Corner. Get there from the lower end of the Grassy Goat Trail.

review.notes: Route Location and area Getting There. No descent source for this route.

set.approach: Follow Fox Creek on its south side past Fox Creek Falls, then climb the ridge north of the falls. At an obvious mud slope, drop down and cross Fox Creek again, then head up and left along a ridge into the bowl that sits between Index and Pilot. Contour across the west side of Index to the foot of the line. The line begins at the only major weakness in the lower headwall; early in the season it is a tongue of snow and ice over a short overhang, later a chimney.
set.descent_text: Two ways off are described. Rappel the north side of the summit and retrace the moves through the rock tunnel to an awkward hanging anchor above the large ledge. Or downclimb the final pitch, from above the crux chimney, scramble southeast to an anchor made from a horn and a beak, and rappel the prow to the ledge. Then rappel to the snow or choss gully, downclimb it, and rappel to the base. Replace cord on old anchors.

review.notes: Route page; area page option B approach; rappel counts omitted.

set.approach: Leave the North Fork Trail where Lizard Head Meadow ends on its west side, roughly a mile past Lonesome Lake going east. Climb a grassy, tree-covered south-facing slope to the foot of the southeast ridge. The ridge can also be reached from the Lizard Head trail or from Bear Lake.
set.descent_text: Go down the fourth-class west ridge to the low notch next to Camel's Hump, then head southwest down third-class gullies to Secluded Lake. Follow the lake's outlet south until it meets the North Fork Trail. The steepest, most exposed part of the west ridge has no fixed anchor for rappelling.

review.notes: Route page; area page agrees the west ridge is the usual descent.

set.approach: From the Big Sandy trailhead, follow the Fremont Trail, then the Hailey Pass Trail, then the Pyramid Lake Trail. Camping is possible beside Pyramid Lake or under the dome itself. From the south side of the dome, hike the talus up and right beneath a black band of rock that crosses the southeast face, to the foot of two parallel left-leaning ramps, where the route begins.
set.descent_text: Descend by the standard walk-off on the north side of the dome, which is third class.

set.approach: From Big Sandy Lake, hike the Jackass Pass trail past the switchbacks, then leave the trail before it crosses North Creek and scramble the hillside west of the trail to the east face. The first pitch climbs the big left-facing dihedral in the left-hand third of the face.
set.descent_text: Walk and scramble off down ledges on the west and south sides.

review.notes: Route page; area page agrees on a west walk-off.

set.approach: From the west, take the South Fork Teton Canyon trailhead, follow the unofficial Roaring Fork trail, then traverse overland to the col between Table Mountain and Peak 10635 and go down along the east face. From the east, use the Cascade Canyon trail and line-of-sight route-finding. The route climbs the three golden headwalls of the south face, starting a short way southwest of Heartbreak Ridge.

review.notes: Area approaches and route Location. Descent from the summit not stated.

set.approach: Approach from the west by the South Fork Teton Canyon trailhead and the unofficial Roaring Fork trail, then cross to the col between Table Mountain and Peak 10635 and go down along the east face; or from the east by the Cascade Canyon trail. The ridge is the right (north) boundary of the striking Southeast Couloir. Begin near the toe of the ridge on its right side.
set.descent_text: From the summit, return toward Teton Canyon by the Face Trail or the Huckleberry Trail. Parties heading back to Cascade Canyon must find their own way.

set.approach: Reach the Cirque of the Towers by Jackass Pass from the Big Sandy trailhead. The route is low on the northeast face of The Plume above Arrowhead Lake. The first pitch follows a textured black streak at the spot where the climbers' trail from Arrowhead Lake toward the western variant of Jackass Pass meets the wall, well left and below the Roof of Tears corner.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. The lower rappels end by going down to climber's left on ledges to the talus; do not reverse the first three pitches.

review.notes: Route page Location and Descent; area page for Jackass Pass.
